dedupe_keys.name: edgartools python library for sec edgar filings and xbrl data

description: EdgarTools is a Python library for accessing and analysing filings in the US Securities and Exchange Commission's EDGAR system. It retrieves company data such as shares outstanding and public float, parses XBRL financial statements from 10-K and 10-Q filings with multi-period stitching and standardised concept labels, reads insider transactions from Forms 3, 4 and 5, extracts executive compensation from proxy statements and analyses investment fund filings, exporting results as pandas DataFrames. It is maintained by Dwight Gunning. Coverage is companies and funds filing with the SEC. It is free and installed with pip; the PyPI package, version 5.59.1 of 26 September 2026, is under the MIT licence, needs Python 3.10 or later, and is marked beta. Users must declare an identity to the SEC before making requests. Caveats: it depends on EDGAR's services and rate limits, and standardised labels map company-specific XBRL tags imperfectly. For simulation it supplies balance sheets and financial statements of listed utilities, banks and industrial firms for financial resilience and contagion models, and filings that describe exposure of companies to disruptions. It is related to the Arelle platform record in this catalogue, which validates the same XBRL filings.
